business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (continental/Napoleonic tradition) with a Common Law-derived corporation statute (Ley 32 de 1927, modernized by Ley 5 de 2024); notarial system governs corporate records and registry filings.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (2012, including Chapter 10 on Investment)
Panama–Spain Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (APPRI)
Panama–Germany Treaty for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
OECD/Council of Europe Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (in force for Panama since December 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 and Ley 129 de 2020) and Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 30 de septiembre de 2015 (AML/CFT regulations); Ley 254 de 28 de octubre de 2021 and Decreto Ejecutivo 475 de 14 de diciembre de 2021 establishing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI/MEF); corporate governance under Ley 5 de 2 de enero de 2024 (Ley General de Sociedades).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: RBF filings are confidential and not publicly searchable; access is limited to the DGI, the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and other competent authorities, and information may be exchanged under CRS/Economic Inclusion and Double Taxation Agreement channels.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each subscriber/director/beneficial owner (certified by the origin-country notary or issuing authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or qualified notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Contracting State with effect from 30 November 2017); consular legalization applies only for non-Hague-Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the resident agent and authorizing execution and registration of the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin (official notarial transcript)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if origin is a non-Hague State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Extract and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder owning 10% or more of the future Panama S.A.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Panamanian consular legalization at the origin if source jurisdiction is not a Hague State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the ultimate beneficial owner(s), supporting standard CDD and future KYC onboarding of Wise B2B and Payoneer corporate accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying regulated financial institution in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in origin and apostilled (or consular-legalized where notarial acknowledgment applies)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of all shareholders holding 10% or more, officers and directors under Ley 23/2015 and Decreto Ejecutivo 363/2015; screening against the OFAC SDN and Primary Sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists (1267/1988, 1373, 2253), EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, the UAF national warnings, and adverse media sourcing; politically exposed persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence and senior management approval; ISIC 7310 (advertising/SEO localization) is rated Low_Risk_Standard, permitting streamlined CDD only for qualifying thresholds but never waiving UBO disclosure; the complete pre-incorporation CDD file is retained by the resident agent to support subsequent banking/KYC checks for Wise B2B and Payoneer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal de Trámites en Línea and Sistema de Consulta de Entidades Jurídicas of the Registro Público de Panamá (www.registropublico.gob.pa) – online name search, availability certification, and reservation module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name may be registered in Spanish or any foreign language using Latin-script characters; names originating in non-Latin scripts (CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, etc.) must be transliterated/translated into Latin characters, with the Latin rendering being the operative registered name; the legal suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' is mandatory; the name must be distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity or a protected industrial property right under Ley 35 de 1996.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a proposed name as non-distinctive or misleading, the applicant (through its resident agent) may (i) immediately file a new availability request with a modified or supplementary token; or (ii) file a recurso de apelación before the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification, attaching a legal brief demonstrating absence of confusing similarity and, if relevant, the prior written authorization of the competent regulator (SBP, SMV, SSRP, or other ministry); the negative administrative decision may then be challenged through a recurso de reconsideración followed by judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia; reservations are not extendable beyond the 30-day window and lapse automatically, requiring a fresh filing and fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable: a licensed virtual-office arrangement with a physical Panama address (not a P.O. Box) may serve as the registered office and municipal casa de atención for the Municipality of Panama, provided the resident agent's office remains the statutory address for service of process and the digital agency maintains at least one officer, sub-agent or authorized contact person in Panama to receive regulatory correspondence; a purely nominal address without any receiving capability is not permitted for Aviso de Operación purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated at under 10% in the first 12 months for an unlicensed, low-risk ISIC 7310 digital services company, absent adverse UBO/PEP screening results or tax-audit triggers; the DGI may conduct verificación visits under Código Fiscal Artículo 719 and the Municipality of Panama may perform occasional business-license inspections where a physical casa de atención is declared.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for certified translation packages

stage_1.validation_note: Pre-incorporation CDD file is designed to satisfy Registro Público, DGI, UAF, resident-agent obligations, and future Wise B2B/Payoneer KYC onboarding for the App Growth Agency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as substantially amended by Ley No. 3 de 1988 and Ley No. 32 de 2011; formation and registration governed by Articles 1 through 16 of said Law; beneficial-ownership reporting obligations imposed by Ley No. 23 de 2015 and Executive Decree No. 312 de 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Sección Mercantil)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva (Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and enrolled with the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A Sociedad Anónima may incorporate with authorized nominal capital customarily set at USD 10,000, divided into shares with par value, without requiring contribution, escrow, bank certificate, or proof of payment at registration. Shares may be subscribed but unpaid, and non-resident ownership is expressly permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription by the founding subscriber is hereby accepted; the subscribed shares are issued and recorded in the share register and stock certificates. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the office at the resident agent's seat in Panama City is adopted as the registered office, and the resident agent is ratified for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the President, the Secretary and the Treasurer are appointed as officers, each to serve until successors are duly elected. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the officers are authorised to open payment-rail accounts, obtain the municipal operation notice, and execute all incorporation filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search, deed drafting and notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuito de Panamá; licensed Panamanian attorney (abogado) acting as incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-registration name availability search in the Registro Público database to secure a permissible corporate name. Instruct the licensed attorney to draft the Escritura Pública with standard S.A. bylaws, including perpetual duration, territorial tax scope, authorized capital (customarily USD 10,000), object clause covering ISIC 7310 (app store optimization, multilingual organic search and digital marketing services), appointment of the resident agent, initial directors, and general powers. Execute the deed before a Panamanian notary or through the registered agent under the microfilm regime, then obtain notarial protocol copies for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Name availability search request (Solicitud de Búsqueda de Nombre)
Draft of Escritura Pública and Articles of Association
Passport copies and proof of identity of subscribers and first directors
Acceptance letter of the resident agent (Agente Residente)
Client instruction letter identifying shareholders and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration, promptly submit an alternative name and pay the additional search token. If the notary identifies defective clauses, cure by executing a corrective addendum (aclaración) to the deed before registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Banco Nacional de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the fiscal stamp token (pago de timbres) and obtain the DGI endorsement (visto bueno fiscal) on the notarized deed before inscription. Thereafter obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) number for the company and confirm territorial tax classification, under which income derived from services rendered entirely outside Panama, such as foreign-sourced ASO and SEO localization services, falls outside Panamanian income tax. If the company later generates Panamanian-source income, register the applicable tax obligations and invoice requirements with DGI.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública submitted for fiscal endorsement
RUC-11 application form (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Passport or identity card of the legal representative
Receipt of payment of fiscal stamps from Banco Nacional de Panamá
Statement confirming territorial source of income and foreign-service business model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is queried, correct discrepancies at the DGI taxpayer assistance windows or through the online updater. If the fiscal token payment is miscalculated, apply for adjustment or credit at Banco Nacional de Panamá and request a reissued endorsement receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the deed with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Sección Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the original and a copy of the DGI-endorsed Escritura Pública to the Public Registry for inscription (inscripción). The Registry reviews the legality and form of the deed, assigns a corporate file number (ficha), and issues the inscription certificate (Copia Literal Inscrita) evidencing the company's formation date. Request the Certificado de Persona Jurídica, which is the standard certified corporate document used for banking and payment-rail onboarding.
required_dossiers: DGI-endorsed notarial deed in original plus one copy
Receipt of payment of the Public Registry inscription fee
Registry transmittal cover form with applicant details
Apostilled or legalized proof of identity of foreign subscribers if required by registry practice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry files an objection (razón) regarding formal or substantive defects, cure the deficiency by filing the corrected documents within the stated period; the attorney may submit a clarifying addendum. Where time is critical, request expedited review at the Registry's fast-track window and follow up until the inscription certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation corporate governance and statutory books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and the resident agent at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formalize corporate existence by authenticating the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, appointing President, Secretary and Treasurer, issuing share certificates, and opening the share register and minutes book. Obtain the Certificación de Cargos (certificate of officers) and the Registered Agent Certificate from the resident agent. The resident agent must also file the beneficial ownership declaration required by Ley No. 23 de 2015 within the statutory period, identifying the ultimate natural persons behind the company.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution signed by the directors
Share subscription and allocation forms executed by the founding subscriber
Share certificates signed by the President and Secretary
Share register and minutes book
Beneficial ownership information sheets and UBO declarations under Ley No. 23 de 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes or allotment forms contain formal defects, re-execute by unanimous written resolution with retroactive consent. If officers change, obtain a revised Certificación de Cargos from the registered agent and ensure the registry and banking counterparts are updated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating notice and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Aviso de Operación; Caja de Seguro Social; Cuerpo de Bomberos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the annual municipal Aviso de Operación covering the service activity of advertising and digital marketing (ISIC 7310). Where a physical office is opened in Panama, complete the municipal inspection and obtain the fire-safety clearance from the Cuerpo de Bomberos. If local employees are retained, register with the Caja de Seguro Social and the DGI payroll withholding system. For purely digital services rendered to foreign clients, the municipal tax base remains territorial and the Aviso de Operación is nonetheless mandatory where any physical or virtual office presence exists in the municipality.
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription and Certificado de Persona Jurídica
RUC certificate and taxpayer identification
Identity documents of the legal representative and officers
Lease or right-of-use agreement for the physical office, if applicable
CSS employer registration forms and employee records, if hiring locally
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects to the application, submit a supplementary declaration of gross receipts, clarify the territorial source of income, and use the municipal changes form to amend the license class. Disputes over assessed fees may be appealed to the Dirección de Ingresos Municipales.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership filing, corporate certification and payment-rail onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Beneficial Ownership Registry); Wise B2B and Payoneer compliance teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the resident agent files the final beneficial ownership record with the Public Registry portal within the statutory deadline and maintains the certified corporate file. With the complete corporate kit, open Wise B2B and Payoneer business accounts for the S.A., submitting the KYC/AML documentation, W-8BEN-E or equivalent tax forms, and the board resolution designating the authorized signatories. Provide the First Board Resolution, officer certificate and share register as evidence of valid corporate existence and governance.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificado de Persona Jurídica
Certificación de Cargos (officers certificate)
Passport copies of beneficial owners and the beneficial ownership declaration
Board resolution authorizing opening of payment-rail and bank accounts
W-8BEN-E or FATCA forms as requested by payment providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is queried by the Registry, correct the nationality or ownership data and re-certify through the registered agent. If a financial institution rejects the application, furnish an enhanced due diligence pack through the resident agent and resubmit to alternative payment-rail providers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Aviso de Operación; Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) retains sectoral oversight only for conventional advertising services involving regulated media; digital-only ASO and SEO localization services require no sectoral industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice) and Fire-Safety Clearance Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category III (digital service operation with no significant environmental impact); no EIA study or registration requirement for low-risk office-based commercial services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a software-based ASO and SEO localization operation; general compliance with Law No. 41 de 1998 (Ley General de Ambiente) and municipal solid waste ordinances is required. No wastewater, VOC, or industrial discharge thresholds arise from the business activity; small electronic waste from office equipment must be handled by authorized municipal or private collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá: fire-prevention certificate covering extinguishers, emergency exits, evacuation plans and electrical load safety; Municipality of Panama: structural and occupancy clearance for any leased office space; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral: compliance with workplace health-and-safety regulations and employee accident registration, together with Caja de Seguro Social employer registration, whenever local personnel are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portal: Sistema T@X (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa); e-invoicing clearance platform: Portal de Facturación Electrónica de la DGI; auxiliary registry: Municipio de Panamá (Aviso de Operación) and Registro Público de Panamá (corporate registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima at the Registro Público de Panamá (commercial registry, foil identification) and obtain the Certificado de Registro. Step 2: Obtain a municipal Aviso de Operación at the Municipalidad where the registered office is located. Step 3: File Form 'Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente' with the DGI through the T@X portal (or physically at the DGI Customer Service branches), attaching the public deed, corporate certificate, proof of registered office, identification of directors/resident agent, and municipal notice. Step 4: The DGI issues the legal-entity RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) under the format 9-XX-XXXXXX or successor 11-digit format. Step 5: Apply for a qualified digital signature (Firma Electrónica Calificada) from a DGI-authorized certification authority to activate mandatory e-invoicing. Step 6: Complete the DGI's e-invoicing registration via the Facturación Electrónica module, selecting the online (SFE) or offline billing modality. Step 7: Obtain ITBMS inscription with activity classification corresponding to services under ISIC 7310/NAICS 541810; the DGI then activates the zero-rating/export service procedures upon filing of the export service declaration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Panama-source income only, territorial scope; no pass-through eligibility). The S.A. is a resident juridical person subject to corporation income tax (ISR) at progressive rates from 15% to 25% solely on income from Panamanian source. Income derived from services rendered and effectively used entirely outside Panama falls outside the territorial net and is not taxable in Panama. The SEO/ASO localization agency model remains carefully boundary-tested because services encoded as 'performed in Panama' may be treated as Panama-source even if the customer is abroad.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box or any elective hybrid-mismatch regime. Statutory elections available to the S.A. include: (a) election between the 'coeficiente' (prior-year turnover ratio) and 'rentas estimadas' (estimated-profit) methods for quarterly advance ISR payments under Código Fiscal Art. 733; (b) election to apply the simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' invoicing/ITBMS regime where annual gross income does not exceed B/.36,000; (c) election to obtain 'Bono de Inversión' or accelerated depreciation for qualifying technology investment under Law 52 of 2019; (d) election under the SEM (Sede de Empresa Multinacional) regime under Law 41 of 2007 to lock in territorial treatment and special ITBMS export exemptions for intra-group service hubs; (e) election to pay the 10% shareholder-profit surcharge versus full dividend distribution treatment; tax consolidation is not permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panama's value-added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary de-minimis threshold; ITBMS registration is mandatory for any person or legal entity habitually carrying out taxable commercial activities within the territory. The DGI requires registration of the RUC before the first invoice is issued. Foreign non-resident providers of digital services (including ASO/SEO platform services) create an ITBMS nexus when customers are located in Panama; foreign digital suppliers may be required to register through a legal representative under Decreto Ejecutivo 2 de 2022 where digital services are rendered to Panamanian consumers. Small domestic businesses with annual gross receipts not exceeding B/.36,000 may opt into the simplified peqeño contribuyente regime (which excludes certain ITBMS mechanics but does not waive registration).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory under Law 93 of 2019, Executive Decree 26 of 2020, and DGI Resolution 201-3246. All active RUC/ITBMS taxpayers must issue electronic invoices (Factura Electrónica) in XML format with a QR stamp containing the Código de Trazabilidad Fiscal (CTF). Two clearance modalities exist: (i) online real-time API/Web Services transmission through DGI-authorized SFE (Sociedades de Facturación Electrónica); (ii) offline-mode via DGI-approved billing software where invoices are transmitted within 24-48 hours. In both modalities, the DGI validates the invoice, returns a status (Aceptada/Rechazado) and assigns a unique folio. The CTF QR code and digital signature are required for all invoices, receipts, credit notes, and export documents. Taxpayers are also required to file periodic ITBMS declarations (Form 20) and monthly purchase/sales books electronically through the T@X system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Código Fiscal Art. 746-A and supporting regulations (Executive Decree 84 of 2005), a 0% ITBMS rate applies to: (a) tangible goods placed under an export customs regime, and (b) exported services rendered to clients domiciled, established or resident abroad, where the services are effectively used or exploited outside Panama. For the App Growth Agency (ISIC 7310/NAICS 541810), zero-rating requires: a written export service contract with a non-resident principal; the issuance of an electronic export invoice (with the QR/CTF code and annotation 'Exportación de Servicios'); deliverables demonstrably consumed abroad (campaign management, multilingual organic search, supplier outreach, App Store/ASO ranking services); and receipt of the consideration from foreign payment rails (Wise B2B, Payoneer, correspondent bank transfers) in a Panamanian bank account or licensed electronic-money account. The 0% rate preserves the right to full ITBMS input-tax credit or refund on local purchases used for the exported services. For income tax purposes, the corresponding service income is treated as foreign-source only where the DGI's source rules (Código Fiscal Art. 694 and DE 44 of 2019) are satisfied; to mitigate reclassification risk, the agency should maintain substance documentation and, where a multinational group is present, consider the SEM regime for definitive territorial exclusion.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUI (Documento Único de Aduanas) or electronic export declaration showing 'Exportación' status for physical goods, if any
Export service contract/invoice (electronic invoice with QR/CTF code annotated 'Exportación de Servicios')

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical exports; for services, a delivery and usage report including campaign logs, geo-targeting evidence, App Store/Google Play store identify evidence, and client acceptance certificates
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement from a Panamanian bank evidencing receipt in USD of the export consideration, or SWIFT/MT103, along with Wise B2B / Payoneer settlement records
RUC certificate, Aviso de Operación, and DGI export-service declaration (Form 20 annex) and any applicable SEM/export services certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits exporters under the 'Fiscalización al Sector Exportador' program. If the zero-rating is disallowed or documentation is deficient, the ITBMS is clawed back at 7% retroactively from the invoice date, plus statoll monthly interest (1.5% per month, capped as provided by law), a 10% 'recargo' surcharge, and fines under Código Fiscal Arts. 758-760 ranging from B/.500 to B/.20,000. Recurrent or fraudulent export zero-rating is classified as tax evasion under Law 70 of 2019 (Código Fiscal/Procedural) and may be prosecuted criminally with penalties of 2-5 years imprisonment for amounts above B/.50,000, exclusion from export-benefit regimes for five years, restitution of input VAT refunds, and administrative disqualification of directors/resident agents involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the sole banking and liquidity regulator under Decree-Law 9 of 1998; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent and agent bank of the State; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), operating under the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, supervises AML/CFT compliance. Panama has no central bank, no currency board, and no foreign-exchange control authority; monetary anchoring is supplied by the United States Federal Reserve through Panama's full dollarization regime established in 1904.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Absolute de facto and de jure convertibility. The US Dollar is legal tender and circulates freely at par with the balboa (PAB), which exists only as fractional coins and has no independent exchange market. There are no capital-account controls, no current-account restrictions, no advance approvals for foreign investments, and no profit-remittance licensing. A Panamanian S.A. may inject capital, repatriate dividends, pay management or intercompany fees, and service shareholder loans to non-residents by ordinary SWIFT USD transfers without central-bank clearance. The only operational hurdles are bank-level enhanced due diligence, the UAF final-beneficiary disclosure framework, and tax-stage rules such as the 10% dividend withholding tax applicable to distributions from Panama-source profits to non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds. This rule is structurally moot because the balboa is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar and no paper balboa circulates; export receipts in USD are already domestic legal tender. For an ASO/SEO localization agency exporting digital services, incoming foreign remittances are classified as ordinary commercial credits and the receiving bank may require only an export invoice, a master service agreement, and a purpose code for AML documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (segregated Capital Escrow Account available for paid-in capital)
Operational Account (fiscal agent; no dedicated corporate escrow product)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as a secondary settlement rail but Low as a standalone treasury anchor. Wise B2B and Payoneer are foreign electronic money institutions / money services businesses, not SBP-licensed banks, and they cannot accept Panamanian retail deposits or offer Panamanian deposit protection. Wise B2B can onboard the Panamanian S.A. but applies its own 'digital marketing' handling rules and may demand a non-registered-agent physical operating address, UBO identity documentation, and executed client service agreements before enabling multi-currency receiving balances in USD, EUR, and GBP. Payoneer expressly supports Panama-registered service exporters for marketplace payouts. Legal constraint: neither EMI qualifies as the primary corporate bank for statutory audit evidence, escrow duties, or client-money segregation; both may hold only short-term settlement float and must be swept daily into the SBP-regulated operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto mandate for Tier-1 banks. For a 100% non-resident-owned S.A. engaged in digital agency services, at least one natural-person director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) should appear physically in Panama City for the account-opening interview, or, at minimum, complete a live video interview supported by apostilled corporate documents, a Panama-licensed attorney acting as KYC presenter, and a prior-bank reference. Panama's post-FATF-greylist compliance practice (in force since October 2023) has materially hardened identification obligations under Law 23/2015, as amended by Law 70/2019, and subsequent SBP implementing regulations. Fully remote account opening is denied or indefinitely deferred unless the structure is assessed as low risk and the bank enjoys an established relationship with the presenting counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with no local executive presence or economic substance (tax-haven typology).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Resident-agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm; notarized shareholders' and directors' resolutions appointing local signatories; UBO affidavit (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) filed with the UAF; annual Aviso de Operación; a physical or virtual office service agreement in Panama; and a professional bank reference from the controlling shareholder's home-country institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity digital-marketing receivables without visible deliverables (invoicing-without-substance pattern).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements for each ASO/SEO client; itemized multilingual localization vendor invoices; App Store Connect and Google Play Console performance dashboards reconciling platform payouts to invoices; a workflow narrative from client purchase order to campaign delivery; and monthly management accounts prepared by a licensed Panamanian public accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inflows from payment intermediaries (Wise B2B, Payoneer, Stripe) matching collection-through-intermediary money-laundering typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EMI payout statements showing merchant and publisher identification; payout contracts with app publishers; SWIFT MT103 references when funds are forwarded from the EMI's account to the Panamanian bank; and a written representation that the agency model involves no anonymous clients, no cash payments, no third-party fund cashing, and no commingling of client funds with operating funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share legacy, nominee opacity, or inadvertent client-money commingling on a single operating account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current share register showing registered shares with no bearer instruments; certified Certificado de Acciones; cancellation and immobilization evidence for any pre-2015 bearer instruments; final-beneficiary registry receipt from the UAF; and an accounting policy that client funds never transit the agency's operating account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection: SWIFT MT103 transfer from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Panamanian operating or capital escrow account, using Field 70 reference 'Aporte de Capital – PA_CORP' and ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (Equity Investment). The receiving bank will require the capital-increase board resolution, a notarized share subscription list, the updated share register, and a source-of-funds statement from the remitting shareholder. Shareholder loans must be identified with purpose code LOAN and supported by a signed intercompany loan agreement containing arm's-length interest and a repayment schedule. No Panamanian FX or central-bank authorization is required; aggregate inbound wires above USD 50,000 per month may trigger enhanced due diligence, and all corporate filings must remain consistent with the UAF beneficial-ownership record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements: (i) ordinary localization and ASO vendor invoices below USD 50,000 are cleared by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code SERV (Services); (ii) campaign procurement above USD 50,000 or high-value platform contracts are routed through an irrevocable at-sight commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by the Tier-1 bank to the vendor's bank, or through a documentary collection under URC 522; (iii) same-day USD disbursements to Panamanian contractors use the local automated clearing house (ACH) accessible through Banco General, BAC International Bank, Banistmo, or Multibank; (iv) multi-currency compensation to overseas SEO and translation staff is executed as MT103 in EUR or GBP, sourced under the FX forward hedging program to lock the USD cost basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) with tenors of 1 to 12 months, executed under the SBP-regulated bank's ISDA/CSA framework and governed by a non-speculative treasury policy
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) to align operating liquidity with supplier-currency liabilities and balance-sheet exposures
OTC vanilla FX options (EUR/USD and GBP/USD calls and puts) for premium-capped, risk-managed hedging of committed foreign-currency vendor obligations
FX swaps (tom/next rollover) to mobilize USD against EUR/GBP settlement balances for short-term liquidity matching

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible or economically meaningful for the PAB/USD pair because Panama is fully dollarized; NDFs on third-country Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) are available from global investment banks but are outside the clearing schema of this agency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 March following the calendar fiscal year; electronic filing may be extended by one month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues default interest of approximately 10% per annum plus a surcharge of 5% of the tax due (minimum USD 50). Persistent non-filing blocks good-standing certificates and may result in administrative strike-off by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Caja General del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on or before 30 June; assessed as a flat fee without a substantive return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a 10% surcharge plus monthly default interest; corporations with an outstanding unpaid tax for three consecutive years may be administratively stricken from the Registro Público de Panamá.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required if gross annual revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 500,000; corporations below both thresholds may prepare unaudited simplified financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Panama Accounting Technical Board; qualifying SMEs may apply the IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO confirmation filing is required under Panamanian law. Resident agents must maintain a current beneficial ownership record at the registered office; a share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and communicated to the resident agent to update the ownership records.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: income sourced within Panama taxed at 25%; foreign-source income generally exempt. No general tax holiday for ASO/SEO service agency. Small taxpayer regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) offers simplified 2% gross receipts tax for qualifying businesses with annual gross income below USD 200,000. No payroll or municipal tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 201 (Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed via Panama's Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax system 'Sistema T@x-Pay'
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline on or before the third month after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for calendar year-end companies). For non-resident corporations with a Panama registered agent, the deadline is based on the corporate fiscal year; tax payments are due in three monthly installments starting in the fourth month after year-end (June, July, August for calendar year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panama-source commercial, industrial, and service activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source revenue; foreign revenue is excluded under territorial taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable foreign-source income and other exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting evidence of foreign-source characterization (e.g., service contracts, client invoices, proof of performance outside Panama).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses directly incurred in generating Panama-source revenue; allocate common expenses reasonably.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income before deductions and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute as Panama-source gross revenue less allowable deductions and exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax rate and total income tax due (25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% to Panama-source taxable income. Tax credits for advance payments and withholdings may be applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholdings, and tax credits (e.g., 2% advance on gross Panama-source revenue; 1.5% bank debit tax credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only taxes paid to Panama DGI or withheld by Panama payers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refund request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source activity, file zero return with all revenue and income reported as foreign-source, subject to DGI audit verification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 50%. Interest accrues at the statutory rate (currently 1% per month). Failure to file zero returns: fixed penalty of USD 20 to USD 50. Failure to pay tax: surcharge of 1% per month plus interest. Underreported tax: penalty of 10% of the omitted amount. Non-filing of Form 201 may also trigger suspension of the corporation's Panama operating license and foreign trade privileges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed from Panama-source earnings. Dividends paid from a Panama corporation's foreign-source earnings are not subject to Panama withholding tax. For dividends distributed by a Panama entity derived from domestic earnings, the company must pay a 10% withholding tax; alternatively, a 20% rate applies if the 40% advance corporate tax credit mechanism is not followed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited (e.g., Mexico, Barbados, UAE, Qatar, South Korea, Portugal, Singapore). To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) submit a Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, legalized/apostilled and translated into Spanish if required; (2) present the TRC to the Panama paying entity or the DGI alongside the dividend payment declaration; (3) file Form 201 Annex D (or the applicable treaty relief form) with the DGI. Panama's DTA rates generally reduce dividend withholding to 5% or 10% depending on ownership thresholds, but only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and meets economic substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate on royalties paid to non-residents: 12.5% on gross royalties from the use of trademarks, patents, software, or industrial know-how in Panama. Treaty rates may reduce royalties to 10% (under certain DTAs). Statutory rate on interest paid to non-residents: 12.5% on gross interest paid by Panama entities to foreign lenders; no withholding on interest paid to recognized financial institutions or on public debt. Treaty rates on interest generally 10%. Cross-border service fees (including ASO/SEO localization services) are typically not subject to Panama withholding tax if the services are rendered abroad and are not considered Panama-source income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No specific statutory threshold expressed in PAB/USD; Panama's transfer pricing rules apply to taxpayers with cross-border transactions with related parties exceeding USD 250,000 per fiscal year. Documentation required: Local File when aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 3 million; Master File when group annual consolidated revenue exceeds USD 50 million. Country-by-Country Report filing required for groups with consolidated revenue of at least USD 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama adopted Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) via Law 254 of 2021, effective for fiscal year 2022. All Panama legal entities engaged in relevant activities (including distribution and service centers, headquarters, and financing activities) must maintain substantial economic presence in Panama. For an ASO/SEO localization agency, the relevant activity is 'service business' if the entity provides services to non-resident affiliates. Essential requirements: (a) core income-generating activities performed in Panama; (b) adequate premises, employees, and equipment in Panama; (c) full compliance with corporate record-keeping. Entities failing ESR must report and pay a tax of 12.5% on total gross income (effective 2021 onward) and may have their corporate registrations suspended. A purely passive or shell corporation engaged in foreign-source ASO/SEO services with no local activity is exposed to ESR penalties and potential recharacterization of income as Panama-source.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source revenue, false invoices, improper deduction claims, or deliberate mischaracterization of local service income as foreign-source income to escape the 25% corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under the Tax Criminal Code (Ley 5 de 2021): imprisonment from 2 to 5 years; monetary fine equal to 50% to 100% of the evaded tax. Administrative penalties: 10% understatement penalty plus monthly surcharge and interest. Bankruptcy or dissolution may be ordered for asset concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and legal representatives who sign fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties. Criminal court may impose travel bans, precautionary banking freezes, and restitution orders. If the company is deemed a facade, courts may pierce the corporate veil to hold personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Violation (Régimen de Sustancia Económica)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Panama-incorporated company performing cross-border ASO/SEO and localization services without maintaining a physical office, local employees, or board meetings in Panama; claiming intermediary status or mere conduit arrangement. Also failures to timely file the annual Tax Information Return (declaración de sustancia económica).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalty: USD 50,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation, plus a special 12.5% tax on all gross income of the entity. Suspension of the corporate legal personality (registro) after 90 days of non-compliance; subsequent cancellation of the registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and resident agents knowingly providing false statements may face fines of USD 10,000 to USD 50,000, disqualification from holding directorships in Panama, and criminal liability for false testimony (up to 2 years imprisonment). Personal liability extends to unpaid ESR special tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Compliance Failure (Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2015)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling client funds through the Panama S.A. bank accounts without implementing a Risk-Based Approach, lacking Customer Due Diligence (CDD), or being used as an unlicensed payment intermediary (e.g., receiving ASO service fees from affiliates and immediately distributing to third parties without economic justification). Failure to report suspicious transactions to UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 for negligent AML compliance. If the entity is used as a vehicle for illicit transfer (e.g., invoicing fraud, VAT evasion, or terrorist financing), the assets are subject to confiscation and the company may be dissolved. Criminal penalties up to 12 years imprisonment for individuals convicted of money laundering under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML program failures. A court may issue a travel ban and freeze personal assets if the director knowingly participated in or permitted laundering through the corporation. Personal criminal liability cannot be indemnified by the corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Penalty / Aggressive Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit the Local File / Master File when related-party cross-border transactions exceed the threshold, or employing a non-arm's-length commission structure for the Panama entity operating as an ASO/SEO agency for foreign affiliates (e.g., inflating cost-plus margin to shift profits abroad).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative adjustment of taxable income plus 20% surcharge on the additional tax due, and monthly interest. If the adjustment stems from hidden transactions or false documentation, the penalty rises to 40% of the omitted tax. Failure to file documentation: USD 30,000 to USD 100,000 per omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who sign tax returns with false transfer pricing documentation may face criminal tax evasion liability. Directors may be subject to a personal liability ruling for the 20%/40% surcharges if they vote to approve fraudulent intercompany invoices.
